correctness.rationale: Checked semantics of μ(t)=∀v ?(v=t): true exactly when the whole team has constant t. Consequently μ(x)→μ(y) is functional dependence x→y under subteam implication, and ∃inq w(w≠z) holds precisely when some z-domain value is absent. Failure of outer implication is an FD-consistent subteam covering every z. For r(X)≤2, Boolean variables per observed (x,y) pair, 0–2-literal coverage clauses and pairwise incompatible-y exclusions yield an exact 2-SAT reduction even with unrestricted y values. The 3-SAT reduction has exactly three distinct rows in every padded clause fibre, y∈{0,1}, and identical universe shared between z,x,y; it maps satisfiability to failure of support, proving coNP hardness with polynomial certificates for the complement. Independent finite constraints and reduction comparisons covered 1,200 instances.
